newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Major shareholder disposes Great Wall shrs.
newsitem.headline: Major shareholder disposes Great Wall shrs.

text.p: Always Keen Ltd, a substantial shareholder of Great Wall Electronic International Ltd, said on Friday it has agreed to sell 323.12 million Great Wall shares it held, or 34.9 percent of the company to Vandor Profits Ltd.

Always keen, which had 39.7 percent stake in Great Wall on September 10, would be paid HK$120.3 million in cash and 4,900 new shares of US$1 each in Vandor, representing an estimated HK$0.73 per each for the Great Wall shares, it said.
The selling price was at a premium of 32.7 percent over their Tuesday close of HK$0.55 per share before trading was suspended on Wednesday pending an announcement.
Always Keen said it would have a 49 percent interest in Vandor while Vandor's existing parent Macross Profits Ltd's stake would be diluted to 51 percent after the transaction.

Always Keen also agreed to place its remaining 44.54 million shares in Great Wall to private investors at HK$0.45 per share, or a 18 percent discount to the shares' Tuesday close of HK$0.55, the company said.
After the transaction and placement Great Wall would be 34.9 percent held by Vandor, 11 percent by Franklin Resources Inc, 49.3 percent by public shareholders and 4.8 percent by placees, it said.
Macross, which was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands in July, 1996, is a private company owned 60 percent by Wu Shaozhang and 40 percent by Chen Weixiong.
It has carried out no other activities since incorporation. It would be the holding company after the completion of the Great Wall transaction, Macross said in the joint statement.
Wu and Chen would be appointed as executive directors of Great Wall, replacing Tse Wai King and Chiang Yu Hin, who intended to resign.
